title: Lower semicontinuity of fibre dimension for flat finitely presented algebraic spaces
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For $t\in T$ put $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$, using the residue field and its canonical point map [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Define $n_f(t)$ as the supremum of the topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of all affine schemes with a representable etale map to $X_t$; the empty fibre has dimension $-\infty$. Assume $f$ is flat and of finite presentation: flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and finite presentation additionally requires quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Here quasi-compactness means that pullback to a quasi-compact scheme has a quasi-compact scheme atlas, and quasi-separatedness means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Then $n_f(t)\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots\}$ for every $t$, and for each integer $a\geq-1$ the set $\{t\in T:n_f(t)>a\}$ is open. No properness, nonemptiness or equidimensionality assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D4P (lemma-dimension-fibres-flat), restricted to a scheme target; fibre dimension is computed on affine etale charts.

proof.text: Cover $T$ by affine opens $V$. The pullback $X_V=X\times_TV$ has a quasi-compact scheme atlas by the quasi-compactness hypothesis on $f$. By [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement] choose a representable surjective etale map $p:U\to X_V$ with $U$ affine. View $U\to X$ as an etale chart lying above the etale target chart $V\to T$. The hypothesis that flatness and local finite presentation are tested on compatible etale scheme charts says directly that $g:U\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. No composition or descent theorem for flatness is being presumed here. For $t\in V$, fibre-product pasting identifies $(X_V)_t$ with $X_t$ and the base-changed atlas $p_t:U_t\to X_t$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The pointwise statements over $V$ therefore concern the original fibres.

source.place: Tag 0D4P, lemma-dimension-fibres-flat, scheme-target and affine-source reduction

proof.text: We verify the dimension convention rather than assuming it. Write $d_t=\dim|X_t|$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-atlas-topological-dimension] with $B=T$, the original quasi-separated $f$, and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$: it gives $d_t=\dim U_t$. The scheme $U_t$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], since $U,V$ are affine. Thus $U_t$ itself is among the affine charts whose dimensions define $n_f(t)$, giving $d_t\leq n_f(t)$. Conversely, for any affine etale chart $W\to X_t$, form the scheme atlas $W\amalg U_t\to X_t$. This is etale because each scheme test is the disjoint union of the two etale projections, and is surjective because its second summand is. The finite coproduct construction is [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum]; its two summands are open (the two complementary idempotents in the product ring give their principal opens). The same atlas-dimension lemma and [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] give $\dim W\leq\dim(W\amalg U_t)=d_t$. Taking the supremum proves $n_f(t)=d_t=\dim U_t$, including the empty case.

source.place: Tag 0D4P, lemma-dimension-fibres-flat, scheme-target and affine-source reduction

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], the ring map $A\to B$ for $g:U\to V$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, has a presentation $B=A[z_1,\ldots,z_r]/(h_1,\ldots,h_s)$. Let $V'=\operatorname{Spec}A'\subseteq V$ be any affine open. Its preimage $g^{-1}(V')$ is the fibre product $U\times_VV'$ (an open immersion pulls back to the inclusion of the preimage), which is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AA')$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Hence $g$ is affine in the sense of [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $B\otimes_AA'$ is generated as an $A'$-algebra by the finitely many images $z_i\otimes1$, so $g$ is locally of finite type in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3), $g$ is quasi-compact; it is of finite type. The affine base $V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to obtain an integer bound on every $\dim U_t$. Together with step 2 this proves the asserted value range: a nonempty fibre has a finite nonnegative integer dimension and an empty one has $-\infty$.

Fix $t\in V$ with $n_f(t)=n>a$, where $a\geq-1$. By step 3, $n\geq0$. The fibre $U_t$ is a finite type scheme over $\kappa(t)$: its affine ring is obtained from the displayed finite presentation by tensoring with $\kappa(t)$ and has the same finite list of algebra generators. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions], some point $x$ has $\dim_x U_t=n$; a supremum of nonnegative integers bounded by the integer $n$ and equal to $n$ must attain $n$. By [lem-trf-locally-algebraic-dimension-components] choose a component $C$ through $x$ of dimension $n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] it has a generic point $\eta$. Any irreducible component containing $\eta$ contains $\overline{\{\eta\}}=C$ and therefore equals $C$ by maximality. Applying the same component-dimension formula at $\eta$ gives $\dim_\eta U_t=\dim C=n$.

source.place: Tag 0D4H (lemma-dimension-fibres-flat), point in the dimension-n piece; expanded using varieties.tex Tag 0B1B (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic, item-dimension-irreducibles-passing-through)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-flat-fibre-dimension-strata] to $g:U\to V$ and the whole open $V$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1. The point $\eta$ is generic in a component of its ordinary fibre by step 4, so it lies in one of the opens $H_m\subseteq U$ supplied there. Its local fibre dimension is both $m$ and $n$, so $m=n$. Let $N=g(H_n)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], $g$ is an open map, hence $N$ is an open neighbourhood of $t$ in $V$. For $s\in N$, choose $y\in H_n$ with $g(y)=s$. The strata statement gives $\dim_y U_s=n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions], $\dim U_s\geq n>a$. Step 2 identifies this with $n_f(s)$. Thus $N\subseteq\{s:n_f(s)>a\}$.

source.place: Tag 0D4H (lemma-dimension-fibres-flat), constant dimension opens and their images; Tags 054T and 054U for the generic-point opens; morphisms.tex Tag 01UA (lemma-fppf-open)

proof.text: For each affine $V\subseteq T$, step 5 supplies an open neighbourhood inside the strict superlevel set at every point of that set in $V$. Therefore its intersection with $V$ is open in $V$. Since $V$ is open in $T$ and these affine opens cover $T$, the strict superlevel set is their union of such neighbourhoods and is open in $T$. When $a=-1$ this is precisely the nonempty-fibre locus; empty fibres contribute no points. If $T$ is empty all assertions are vacuous. The value-range assertion is also local on this cover, so step 3 proves it on all of $T$.

lean.statement: theorem affineEtaleFibreDimension_finite_isOpen_of_flat {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (T : Over S) (f : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hflat : MapToSchemeIsLocally (@Flat) X T f) (hlfp : MapToSchemeIsLocally (@LocallyOfFinitePresentation) X T f) (hqc : MapIsQuasiCompact f) (hqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal f)) : (∀ t : T.left, affineEtaleFibreDimension X T f t = ⊥ ∨ ∃ n : ℕ, affineEtaleFibreDimension X T f t = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ (∀ a : ℤ, -1 ≤ a → IsOpen {t : T.left | ((a + 1).toNat : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ affineEtaleFibreDimension X T f t})
